answer: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease when their estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is at least 20 mL/min/1.73m² [ADA, 2024]. This recommendation aims to reduce the progression of chronic kidney disease and lower cardiovascular risk. ACE inhibitors or ARBs are typically the first-line treatment for patients with albuminuria and hypertension.

results.content: In patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, an SGLT2 inhibitor is recommended for those with eGFR >=20 mL/min/1.73m2 to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular risk. ACE inhibitors or ARBs are first-line for patients with albuminuria and hypertension.

results.citation: Chronic Kidney Disease in Diabetes, American Diabetes Association, 2024

results.content: Adults with type 2 diabetes should have an annual dilated eye exam for retinopathy, an annual urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio for nephropathy, and an annual comprehensive foot exam with monofilament testing for peripheral neuropathy, starting at diagnosis.
results.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
